practiceQuestions.q: Which Articles of the Indian Constitution enshrine the Right to Freedom?
practiceQuestions.sol: Articles 19 to 22 of the Indian Constitution guarantee the Right to Freedom. Articles 12-35 cover all Fundamental Rights, 23-24 cover Right against Exploitation, and 25-28 cover Right to Freedom of Religion.

practiceQuestions.q: Originally, Article 19 of the Constitution guaranteed how many freedoms?
practiceQuestions.sol: Originally, Article 19 contained seven freedoms. However, the right to property (Article 19(1)(f)) was deleted by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, leaving only six freedoms.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act deleted the right to acquire, hold and dispose of property as a freedom under Article 19?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 removed the right to property from the list of Fundamental Rights under Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31, making it a legal right under Article 300A.

practiceQuestions.q: Protection of life and personal liberty is guaranteed under which Article?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 21 states that no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. This right is available to both citizens and non-citizens.

practiceQuestions.q: The Right to Education (RTE) was added as Article 21A by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 inserted Article 21A, making free and compulsory education for children between the ages of 6 and 14 a fundamental right.

practiceQuestions.q: Article 20 of the Indian Constitution provides protection against which of the following?
opts: Ex-post facto laws, double jeopardy, and self-incrimination
Discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 20 grants protection against arbitrary and excessive punishment to an accused person, encompassing three dimensions: no ex-post-facto law, no double jeopardy, and no self-incrimination.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Article provides protection against arrest and detention in certain cases?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 22 grants protection to persons arrested or detained. It has two parts: the first part deals with ordinary law and the second part deals with preventive detention law.

practiceQuestions.q: Under Article 22, an arrested person must be produced before the nearest magistrate within how many hours, excluding the journey time?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 22(2) mandates that every person who is arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before the nearest magistrate within a period of 24 hours of such arrest, excluding the time necessary for the journey.

practiceQuestions.q: The freedoms guaranteed by Article 19 are available to:
opts: Citizens as well as foreigners except enemy aliens
practiceQuestions.sol: The freedoms under Article 19 are guaranteed only to the citizens of India and are not available to foreigners or legal persons like companies or corporations.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following freedoms is explicitly mentioned under Article 19(1)?
opts: Right to assemble peaceably and without arms
Right to close down business at will
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 19(1)(b) explicitly guarantees the right to assemble peaceably and without arms. Freedom of press is implied under Article 19(1)(a) (freedom of speech and expression), while the right to strike is not a fundamental right.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Supreme Court interpret 'procedure established by law' under Article 21 in light of the post-Maneka Gandhi era?
opts: It is strictly limited to legislative enactment without judicial review of fairness.
It has been read to incorporate 'due process of law', requiring the law to be fair, just, and reasonable.
It applies only during times of National Emergency.
It allows the executive to suspend personal liberty without judicial oversight.
practiceQuestions.sol: In the Maneka Gandhi case (1978), the Supreme Court ruled that the 'procedure established by law' under Article 21 must be 'right, just and fair' and not arbitrary, fanciful, or oppressive, thereby importing the American concept of 'due process of law'.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary constitutional distinction between Article 19 and Article 21 regarding their suspension during a National Emergency?
opts: Both are automatically suspended during any type of emergency.
Article 19 is automatically suspended only for external aggression, while Article 21 can never be suspended.
Article 19 is automatically suspended only during a war or external aggression, whereas Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended even during an emergency.
Article 21 is suspended by presidential order, but Article 19 requires a constitutional amendment.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 358, Article 19 is automatically suspended only when a National Emergency is declared on the grounds of war or external aggression. Per the 44th Amendment Act, rights guaranteed by Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are the grounds for imposing reasonable restrictions on Article 19 freedoms exhaustive and specific?
opts: To prevent executive overreach and arbitrary curtailment of civil liberties by the state.
To allow the judiciary absolute power to rewrite fundamental rights.
To make it impossible for Parliament to pass any criminal legislation.
To restrict civil liberties only during financial emergencies.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constitution explicitly lists the grounds (sovereignty and integrity of India, security of the State, friendly relations with foreign states, public order, decency or morality, contempt of court, defamation, or incitement to an offence) to ensure that the legislature cannot impose arbitrary restrictions beyond these parameters.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the critical distinction between 'Preventive Detention' and 'Punitive Detention' under Indian Constitutional law?
opts: Punitive detention is preventive in nature, while preventive detention occurs after a crime has been proven in court.
Punitive detention punishes a person for a crime committed and proven after trial, whereas preventive detention detains a person to prevent them from committing a crime in the future.
Preventive detention requires a trial before an advisory board, while punitive detention does not require any judicial trial.
There is no constitutional difference between the two terms.
practiceQuestions.sol: Punitive detention is to punish a person for an offense committed after trial and conviction in a court. Preventive detention is designed to prevent a person from committing a crime in the near future, without trial, based on suspicion or apprehension.

practiceQuestions.q: How does Article 20 protect against 'Double Jeopardy'?
opts: It prevents a person from being prosecuted and punished for the same offense more than once.
It prohibits civil suits from being filed if criminal proceedings are already underway.
It ensures that an accused cannot change their plea during trial.
It bars departmental disciplinary action alongside criminal prosecution.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 20(2) states that no person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offense more than once. However, this protection is available only before a court of law or judicial tribunal and does not bar departmental or administrative proceedings.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the scope and limitation of the protection against self-incrimination under Article 20(3)?
opts: An accused person can be compelled to give oral confessions during police interrogation.
Protection applies to compulsory production of documents, thumb impressions, and blood samples.
No person accused of any offense shall be compelled to be a witness against himself, but compulsory collection of material evidence like thumb impressions is permitted.
It applies to civil proceedings and tax recovery assessments as well.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 20(3) protects against testimonial compulsion ('to be a witness against himself'). The Supreme Court has clarified that this does not extend to compulsory exhibition of body, giving thumb impressions, signature, blood, or hair samples.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does the Indian Constitution place restrictions on freedoms under Article 19 in the interest of 'Public Order'?
opts: To suppress peaceful dissent and criticism of government policies.
To maintain public peace, safety, and tranquility, preventing anarchy and violence in society.
To ensure that economic monopolies are protected from competition.
To ban all forms of public gatherings permanently.
practiceQuestions.sol: 'Public order' as a ground for restriction signifies absence of disorder, rioting, or lawlessness. It balances individual liberty with the collective security and peaceful functioning of society.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional significance of the 'Right to Privacy' under Article 21?
opts: It is an absolute right that overrides all state security considerations.
It was recognized as an intrinsic part of the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 by a 9-judge Constitutional Bench.
It is explicitly mentioned as a distinct article alongside Article 21.
It applies only to digital communications and data protection.
practiceQuestions.sol: In Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India (2017), a unanimous 9-judge bench of the Supreme Court held that the Right to Privacy is protected as an intrinsic part of right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 and as a part of the freedoms guaranteed in Part III.

practiceQuestions.q: How does Article 22 regulate the safeguards for individuals detained under preventive detention laws?
opts: Detention can be extended indefinitely without any review by an advisory board.
Detention cannot exceed 3 months unless an advisory board reports sufficient cause for extended detention.
Detainees under preventive laws have the right to legal representation by a lawyer of their choice as a matter of absolute right.
The grounds of detention need never be communicated to the detainee.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 22(4), preventive detention cannot exceed 3 months unless an Advisory Board (composed of high court judges or qualified persons) reports sufficient cause for extension. Also, grounds of detention must be communicated, though disclosure can be withheld if against public interest.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a) considered the bedrock of a democratic polity?
opts: It allows unrestricted defamation and spread of misinformation.
It enables public debate, dissemination of political views, critique of governance, and informed citizen participation necessary for self-government.
It gives citizens the power to overthrow the elected government through armed rebellion.
It exempts citizens from paying taxes on media publications.
practiceQuestions.sol: Freedom of speech and expression is essential for public discourse, democratic accountability, forming public opinion, and individual self-fulfillment, making it vital for a robust democracy.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Right to Freedom under Article 19:
1. The freedoms guaranteed under Article 19 are available to both Indian citizens and foreign nationals residing in India.
2. The state can impose restrictions on the freedom of speech and expression on grounds of 'public order', 'decency or morality', and 'contempt of court'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because freedoms under Article 19 are available *only* to citizens of India and not to foreigners. Statement 2 is correct as Article 19(2) explicitly lists public order, decency/morality, and contempt of court among the permissible grounds for restricting free speech.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 20 of the Constitution:
1. Protection against ex-post-facto criminal legislation applies to both criminal laws and civil tax liabilities.
2. Protection against double jeopardy is available only in proceedings before a court of law or a judicial tribunal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because ex-post-facto law protection under Article 20(1) applies *only* to criminal laws and not to civil laws or tax liabilities (which can be retrospective). Statement 2 is correct; double jeopardy protection under Article 20(2) is restricted to judicial courts or tribunals and does not apply to departmental inquiries.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 21:
1. The right to life includes the right to live with human dignity and environmental protection.
2. Article 21 guarantees protections against arbitrary executive action as well as legislative action.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Supreme Court has expansively interpreted Article 21 to include right to livelihood, clean environment, privacy, medical care, and human dignity. Moreover, following Maneka Gandhi, protection under Article 21 applies against both executive action (if without legal backing) and legislative action (if the law is unjust or unfair).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 22 (Protection against arrest and detention):
1. The right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of one's choice is guaranteed to persons arrested under ordinary criminal law.
2. Persons detained under preventive detention laws have an absolute constitutional right to be represented by a lawyer before the Advisory Board.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Article 22(1) grants arrested persons the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner. Statement 2 is incorrect because Article 22 specifically denies the right to legal representation by a lawyer before the Advisory Board in cases of preventive detention.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the freedoms under Article 19(1)(c):
1. It includes the right to form associations, unions, and cooperative societies.
2. The Supreme Court has held that the right to obtain recognition for an association is a fundamental right under this clause.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Article 19(1)(c) guarantees the right to form associations, unions, or cooperative societies (cooperative societies were added by the 97th Amendment Act, 2011). Statement 2 is incorrect; the Supreme Court has ruled that while forming an association is a fundamental right, getting recognition or a particular status for it is not guaranteed as a fundamental right.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Right to Education under Article 21A:
1. It applies to all children up to the age of 18 years.
2. It was introduced into the Constitution by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Article 21A applies strictly to children between the ages of 6 and 14 years, not 18. Statement 2 is correct; the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002 inserted Article 21A into the Constitution.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the freedom of movement and residence under Article 19(1)(d) and (e):
1. The right of citizens to move freely throughout the territory of India and reside in any part of it is subject to reasonable restrictions for the protection of the interests of any Scheduled Tribe.
2. These freedoms are available to both citizens and foreign nationals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; restrictions can be imposed on movement and residence for the protection of Scheduled Tribes (e.g., Inner Line Permit systems). Statement 2 is incorrect because all freedoms under Article 19 are restricted to citizens of India only.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 19(1)(g) (Freedom of trade and occupation):
1. It includes the right to carry on any trade, business, occupation, or profession.
2. The state is barred from prescribing professional or technical qualifications necessary for practicing any profession.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; Article 19(1)(g) guarantees the right to practice any profession or to carry on any occupation, trade, or business. Statement 2 is incorrect because the state is explicitly empowered under Article 19(6) to prescribe professional or technical qualifications for practicing any profession or carrying on any occupation.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Preventive Detention in India:
1. Both Parliament and State Legislatures have concurrent power to make laws on preventive detention for reasons connected with the security of a State.
2. Preventive detention laws can authorize the detention of a person for an initial period exceeding three months without consulting an Advisory Board.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; under the Seventh Schedule (List III, Entry 3), both Parliament and state legislatures have concurrent power to enact preventive detention laws for reasons connected with security of a state, maintenance of public order, etc. Statement 2 is incorrect because detention beyond three months requires authorization from an Advisory Board; the initial detention without a board cannot exceed three months.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the interrelationship between Article 19, Article 21, and Article 22:
1. A law depriving a person of personal liberty under Article 21 must also satisfy the reasonableness test under Article 19.
2. The Supreme Court in the Cooper case (1970) established that fundamental rights are mutually exclusive and do not overlap.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; following the R.C. Cooper case (1970) and Maneka Gandhi case (1978), it was established that a law impinging on personal liberty under Article 21 must also withstand the test of other fundamental rights like Article 19. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Cooper case explicitly *rejected* the notion that fundamental rights are mutually exclusive, ruling that they overlap and can apply simultaneously.
